lines.say: Big Nate, or Diary of a Wimpy Kid. Every kid who grew up reading picked a side. Most picked wrong.
cap: {o:Big Nate}, or {o:Diary of a Wimpy Kid}.
Every kid who grew up reading picked a side.

lines.say: Big Nate started in nineteen ninety-one, as a daily newspaper comic. Lincoln Peirce drew it every day for thirty-five years.
cap: Lincoln Peirce drew it every day

lines.say: That's thousands of strips, each one built on a setup, a beat, and a punchline. You can feel that discipline in every novel.
cap: each one built on a setup, a beat, and a punchline.
You can feel that {g:discipline} in every novel.

lines.say: Wimpy Kid runs on irony. Greg tells you he's the good guy, and the drawings quietly prove he isn't.
cap: Greg tells you he's the good guy,
and the drawings quietly prove he {r:isn't}.

lines.say: It's clever. But it only works if you read Greg as the joke. And a lot of fans don't.
cap: But it only works if you read Greg as {o:the joke}.

lines.say: Then there's the world. Wimpy Kid orbits Greg. Big Nate is a whole school. Francis, Teddy, Gina, Mrs. Godfrey, each with their own rivalries.
And Nate fails constantly, but he cares. About his comics, his friends, proving people wrong. You root for him, not against him.
cap: And Nate fails constantly, but he {g:cares}.
About his comics, his friends, proving people wrong.

lines.say: So why does Wimpy Kid keep winning the argument? Sales. Over three hundred million copies. But sales measure reach, not quality.
cap: So why does Wimpy Kid keep winning the argument?

lines.say: Then nostalgia. For a lot of people, it was the first big book they finished on their own. And that memory does the arguing.
cap: For a lot of people, it was the first big book

lines.say: And most people read one Big Nate novel from the school library, and never touched the strips, which is where the series actually lives.
cap: And most people read {r:one} Big Nate novel
which is where the series actually lives.

lines.say: Wimpy Kid got a generation reading. Big Nate is the better series. Both can be true.
